paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God wants His people to GROW. The writer says these readers should be teachers by now, but they still need someone to reteach them the basics (Hebrews 5:12). Milk is fine for an infant, but "solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil" (Hebrews 5:14). So the call is to leave the elementary teachings and "go on to maturity" (Hebrews 6:1).

Then the writer gets serious, and I think he does it because he cares. He warns about people who tasted so much of God's goodness and then fell away, and he gives a picture from a field: rain keeps falling, and the land either grows a useful crop or thorns and thistles (Hebrews 6:7-8). Same rain, friend. That tells me what we do with what God gives us matters, and drifting is never standing still. I'd rather hear it from a loving writer now than find out later.

And listen to how he lands it, because this is the good part. He calls them "beloved" and says he's convinced of better things in their case (Hebrews 6:9). "God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name" (Hebrews 6:10). So keep showing diligence to the very end, stay out of the sluggish lane, and follow those who inherit the promises through faith and patience (Hebrews 6:11-12). Keep growing, baker, and keep your ovens warm.
